newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil election bill gets first Congress reading.
newsitem.headline: Brazil election bill gets first Congress reading.

text.p: A bill which would place restrictions on Brazilian President Fernando Henrique Cardoso's unprecedented campaign for re-election next year was given its first reading in Congress Wednesday.
The bill would prevent the president from inaugurating public works in the 90 days before the October 1998 elections, said an aide to Deputy Carlos Apolinario, who drew up the legislation.
Other articles included in the legislation would:
-- stop Cardoso from authorizing transfers of cash to state and municipal governments during the period;
-- restrict his access to television and radio networks;
-- require Cardoso's Brazilian Social Democratic Party to reimburse the presidency for the cost of using official aircraft and other transportation during the run-up to the elections;

-- limit campaign funding by individuals to a maximum of ten percent of their income in the 12 months prior to registration of their donations. Companies would be allowed to donate a maximum of two percent of their turnover.

Approval by Congress earlier this year of a bill allowing holders of executive office to stand for a second consecutive term has opened a debate on what constitutes unfair use of the powers of office by politicians seeking re-election.

The aide to Apolinario said he expected the election rules bill would be put to a vote in the committee next week. Once on the floor of the Chamber of Deputies, government whips would probably try to reduce the restrictions, he said.
The bill must be approved both by houses of parliament by October 3, 12 months before the elections for the presidency, state governorships and many seats in Congress.
